product.toshiba-t5100.creation.fact1: 2 MB validated; optional 4 MB configuration not yet modeled
product.toshiba-t5100.creation.fact2: Blank 40 MB CP-3044-shaped IDE disk, 980/5/17, Setup type 7
product.toshiba-t5100.summary: A landmark 16 MHz 386 portable with EGA-compatible graphics and a four-level plasma display.
product.toshiba-t5100.history: Announced in the United States in September 1987, the T5100 put a desktop-class 16 MHz 80386DX, hard disk and gas-plasma screen into a transportable case. Contemporary reviewers valued its smaller size, standard EGA compatibility, display proportions and keyboard, even while the 20 MHz Compaq Portable 386 was faster. Toshiba offered 40 MB and 100 MB storage variants; the Japanese J-3100SGT family must not be treated as firmware-identical.
product.toshiba-t5100.warning: EXPERIMENTAL: Toshiba BIOS V2.30 boots DOS 3.30 from the internal IDE disk and TESTCE3 4.30 from floppy. The original AGS video ROM is missing, so BluMach adapts a separately supplied IBM EGA ROM in memory. This is a functional compatibility path, not faithful AGS/CELT recovery.
product.toshiba-t5100.technical.market: A high-end transportable business computer, announced in the United States at USD 6,499 and positioned as a desktop-class 80386 system that could travel.
product.toshiba-t5100.technical.commerci: The international baseline used a 16 MHz 80386DX, 2 MB RAM, a 1.44 MB floppy drive and either a 40 MB or 100 MB hard disk. Toshiba documents CP-342/type 6, CP-3044/type 7 and CP30104/type 9 drives. Regional J-3100SGT variants are distinct targets.
product.toshiba-t5100.technical.memory: 2 MB standard with a documented optional 2 MB card. The tested profile provides 640 KB conventional, 1 MB extended and 384 KB LIM memory; 24 bank-0 LIM pages pass a bounded guest probe. The upper EMS allocation and exact gate-array mapping are not modeled.
product.toshiba-t5100.technical.video: The hardware uses Toshiba AGS/CELT logic for EGA/CGA/MDA compatibility and a four-level 640 × 400 gas-plasma panel. The experimental model wraps standard EGA behavior, 256 KB VRAM and 2 KB SRAM with an orange four-level palette. Its guest timing remains 640 × 350 and display switching is incomplete.
product.toshiba-t5100.technical.storage: One internal 1.44 MB floppy drive and an integrated IDE-compatible disk interface. The tested CP-3044 profile uses 980 cylinders, 5 heads and 17 sectors with BIOS type 7. DOS 3.30 FDISK, FORMAT /S, persistent file readback and a cold hard-disk boot pass.
product.toshiba-t5100.technical.firmware: Toshiba system BIOS V2.30 uses 32 KB EVEN 042F and ODD 043F lanes. The missing original 32 KB AGS ROM is represented only by an identified IBM EGA ROM adapted in memory with two observed conservative handoff returns. No firmware is distributed.
product.toshiba-t5100.technical.verified: With 2 MB RAM, internal display, 1.44 MB floppy and the 980/5/17 type-7 disk, Setup is legible, POST reaches 32, Toshiba DOS 3.30 boots from hard disk and read-only TESTCE3 4.30 reaches its main menu. A sampled 1 MB extended-memory test and the 24-page LIM subset also pass.
product.toshiba-t5100.technical.limitati: Original AGS/CELT firmware, exact 640 × 400 scan conversion, gray transfer, internal/external switching, upper EMS, full diagnostics, floppy writes, warm reset/resume and exact Conner timing remain pending. The current result is compatibility-oriented and not cycle accurate.
product.toshiba-t5100.creation.note: Creates the validated experimental 2 MB profile with internal display, one 1.44 MB floppy and a blank 40 MB IDE image. On first boot, open Toshiba Setup, select Internal EGA compatible / External MDA or None, High resolution and hard-disk type 7, then save with F10/Y and power-cycle. Local V2.30 system ROMs and the identified IBM EGA compatibility ROM are required; DOS is not supplied. The 4 MB choice is shown but unavailable until the optional memory card and upper EMS are modeled.
